newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong awards new airport 2nd runway contract.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong awards new airport 2nd runway contract.

text.p: Hong Kong's Airport Authority said it had awarded the contract for the Northern Runway works at the new Chek Lap Kok airport to a consortium comprising AMEC Plc, China Fujian corp and Heilit+Woerner Bau AG.
The HK$995 million (US$128 million) contract will take 19 months to complete, the authority said in a statement on Wednesday.
It includes construction of the airport's second runway and taxi-ways, power and electrical and other systems, and facilities for the Civil Aviation Department and Hong Kong Observatory.

Airport Authority chief executive Henry Townsend said Chek Lap Kok's phase two works, comprising the second runway and an extension to the passenger terminal, would enable the declared runway capacity at the new airport to increase from 37-38 aircraft movements per hour to 50 movements per hour within the first year of commissioning.
The new works would not have any impact on the completion of the first phase of the airport project targeted for completion and opening in April 1998, Townsend said.
The works would be financed through additional borrowing by the authority and would not require any further government support, he added.
